hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y with positive gain (heater warms sensor).
Response has first-order lag of tens of seconds; settling takes several times the initial lag, so a 180s hold may not fully settle.
There is no large dead zone: u=0.5 clearly produces a rise above ambient.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.05 due to heat loss to room.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across u in [0,1].
Steady-state u needed to hold target y=0.5 is in mid-range approx 0.2-0.8.
Sensor noise is small (<0.01) relative to control band width 0.05.

proposal.expected_observation: If positive-gain heater hypothesis is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.05 toward 0.3-0.5 with decreasing slope, staying below 0.6 and showing non-zero end slope if not yet settled.
proposal.readiness_justification: No experiments completed yet, so gain magnitude, lag, u=0 decay rate, linearity, steady-state u for 0.5, and noise are all unresolved; at least 3 experiments including a second amplitude and a u=0 decay are needed before controller design.
proposal.operator_note: First heating test at half power for 180s to measure warming rate, lag and approximate gain.

submission.machine_card: Heater: positive gain, no dead zone. y in [0,1] (0=15C,1=75C), u in [0,1]. Self-draining stable: at u=0 decays from 0.497 to 0.19 in 179s toward ambient ~0.05. Steady model ss(u)~0.05+1.0*u, K~0.9-1.1 linear in 0.4-0.6. Measured equilibria: (0.45,0.497) holds 240s flat; ss(0.5)>0.534 rising; ss(0.4) decaying from 0.534 to 0.491. So u* for y=0.5 is ~0.45-0.46. Lag: tau~150-180s, settling ~600s, initial delay <15s (rise in 6-20s). Speed: ~0.0015-0.002/s mid-range, worst-case 0.006/unit/s. Noise <0.01, quantization step ~0.0054 causing flat 5s slopes. No overshoot tendency if u<=0.70.
submission.design_rationale: First-order self-draining heater with K~1.0, ambient~0.05, tau~150-180s. Measured equilibrium (u=0.45,y~0.497 for 240s in E7-E8) sets feedforward. Brackets ss(0.5)>0.534, ss(0.4)<0.491 imply true u*~0.45-0.46. PI corrects residual: Kp=0.8 gives P~0.36 at 0.45 error for fast warm-up but capped, Ti=160s (Ki=0.005) matches plant tau for stable no-overshoot approach. Umax=0.70 guarantees steady state 0.75-0.80<0.85 soft limit even with +10% gain error, yet reaches band from cold in ~140-170s <300s window. Integral +-0.20 covers >0.10 feedforward error with margin, conditional freeze prevents windup during saturation. 12s low-pass suppresses 0.005 quantization / <0.01 noise without adding lag vs 150s tau.
submission.predicted_behavior: From cold 0.05: saturate at 0.70 for ~60-100s, rise to band in ~140-180s, converge to 0.475-0.525 by ~200-250s, well inside 300s settling window. From near target: settle in 60-120s. Overshoot <0.02 above target (<0.52) in nominal, never exceeds 0.70 power so steady <0.80. Steady duty ~0.45-0.47 with integral trim +-0.05. Ripple <0.01 due to filter. MAE after settling <0.01, time-in-band >95%, energy near minimum (u^2~0.20).
self_test_expectations: control returns finite u in [0,1] for y in [0,1], dt 0.1-5s, first call empty state, no exception
cold y=0.05 target 0.5 gives u=0.70 (capped) not >0.70
near target y=0.497 gives u~0.45-0.50, small P correction
high y=0.80 gives u<=0.20 and cooling (ss<u region)
integral stays within +-0.20 after long hold, no windup during saturation
filtered measurement smooths 0.005 steps, no chatter >0.05 in u per step
submission.operator_note: Controller holds 0.5 C band automatically. Starts with up to 0.70 power when cold then settles near 0.45 power. Keep sensor connected; it filters noise and limits power to 0.70 to stay below overheat limits. Expect in-band within ~3-4 min from cold, then steady with tiny adjustments. No action needed.

submission.diagnosis: Response is slower/laggier, not stronger loss or weaker steady gain. Discovery: u=0.5 rise 0.05->0.18 at 60s, 0.31 at 120s, 0.395 at 180s; cooling tau ~160s; ss(0.45)~0.497 with u*=0.45. Closed-loop with same FF 0.45 settles measured 0.506-0.507 at u 0.448-0.450, i.e. steady gain ~1.0 unchanged, so outflow/gain not shifted. But transient with u=0.7 reaches only 0.237 at 60s, 0.397 at 120s, 0.482 at 180s vs nominal 0.277/0.431 predicted for tau 153s; fit gives tau ~175-193s avg ~185s vs 150-165s nominal (+20-30s, +20%). Same command produces smaller early rise and overshoot 0.53-0.55 persists 300-600s: 0.03 decay takes ~300s implying tau~210s, while KI=0.005 needs 600s to unwind 0.09 integral. Pattern is longer lag producing overshoot and long high tail with unchanged u*, classic response_slower.
submission.change_summary: Lowered warm-up cap 0.70->0.62 to cut overshoot energy for slower plant; sped filter 12s->5s to remove added lag; retuned PI 0.8/0.005 -> 0.65/0.022 with 0.15 limit for 4-5x faster unwind; added measurement-derivative brake KD=12 clamped to +/-0.10; added slow adaptive feedforward ff init tgt-0.05 that low-passes toward applied u with 120s time constant when |err|<0.05, frozen otherwise, so u* is re-learned for nominal 0.45 and changed plant without windup during warm-up.
submission.machine_card: Heater y in [0,1], u in [0,1]. Nominal ss~0.05+1.0*u, u*(0.5)~0.45, tau~150-165s, delay <15s, noise/quant ~0.005. Changed: tau~185-195s (+~25%), gain/ambient approx unchanged, u* still ~0.45. Controller must warm with cap ~0.62, brake approach, integrate ~4-5x faster with anti-windup, adapt ff slowly.
submission.design_rationale: Old tail needs ~600s to remove 0.09 integral at KI=0.005 with err~-0.03. KI=0.022 removes same in ~130s. Lower cap reduces steady-state driving the overshoot: ss(0.62)=0.67 vs ss(0.70)=0.75, so peak drops ~0.02. Filter 5s halves added sensing lag while still smoothing 0.005 quantization. D=KD*dyf (~0.018 braking at 0.0015/s) anticipates arrival and is clamped for noise. Adaptive ff does not integrate when far, only learns settled u, so nominal (0.45 holds 0.497) and slower plant (0.448 holds 0.507) both converge without breaking nominal. Conditional freeze on saturation prevents windup; safety cut at 0.80 retained.
submission.predicted_behavior: Cold start 0.05->0.5: u=0.62 capped until y~0.24 then proportional ease plus D brake; cross 0.475 at ~180s nominal / ~210s slow, peak <0.515 nominal / <0.525 slow, re-enter band within ~80s of peak, stay in band after ~300s with in-band >0.85 after 300s, MAE <0.015, steady u~0.45 nominal / ~0.45 slow with err <0.01. No hard violations or overrides.

submission.diagnosis: Same command now rises slower and stays high longer with unchanged steady-state duty, i.e. increased lag. Cold heating with u=0.70 reaches y~0.235 at 60s vs 0.281 predicted for nominal K=1.0 tau=154s (0.046 low); v1 decay from 0.5385 at 300s (u~0.497) to 0.522 at 600s (u~0.456) is 0.016 over 300s vs 0.028 to 0.510 expected for tau=154s, implying tau_post~350-430s (factor ~2.3). Initial movement slips from ~6-9s in E1 to ~18-24s in heldout. Steady-state duty unchanged: v1 settles u~0.448 to y~0.507 vs nominal ss(0.45)~0.497. Cooling at u~0.31 falls -0.00084 to -0.00090/s matching nominal -0.00089/s, so loss/gain not increased/decreased. With PID tuned for tau~150s the extra lag produces prolonged above-band hold (v1 in-band 0.56, y 0.53-0.55 for 200-500s) and, with FF tracking u when |err|<0.05 tau120s, FF is dragged 0.45->~0.53 during approach causing v2 limit cycle 0.43-0.59 period ~500s and late mean 0.559 at u 0.477.
submission.change_summary: Lowered loop aggressiveness for larger lag and fixed feedforward wind-up. Kp 0.65->0.50, Ki 0.022->0.010, Kd 12.0->3.0 with D-limit 0.10->0.06, I-limit 0.15->0.12, U_MAX 0.62->0.70. Kept fast filter tau 4s, added slow filter tau 20s for derivative and adaptation. Changed FF adaptation from |err|<0.05 with tau 120s tracking u unconditionally to |err|<0.025 AND |dy_slow|<0.0007 with tau 250s, so FF only learns steady-state duty when inside band and settled. This stops FF being dragged from 0.45 toward 0.60 during approach (cause of v1 prolonged 0.53-0.54 hold and v2 0.43-0.59 limit cycle) while still allowing u* to re-estimate if plant gain/ambient shifts. Kept anti-windup freeze on saturation and 0.68/0.80 safety caps.
submission.machine_card: Nominal: first-order heater y in [0,1], ss(u)~0.05+1.0*u, u*(0.5)~0.45, tau_cool~154s from E3 (0.497->0.19 in 179s), delay <10s, quant ~0.005 noise <0.01. Degraded (inferred): same K~1.0 and ambient~0.05 (u*~0.44-0.46 still holds 0.50), effective tau~300-430s plus ~8-10s extra dead-time. Evidence: 60s heating deficit 0.046, 300s decay half-rate, 18s start delay, unchanged cooling slope, unchanged late (u,y) pair.
submission.design_rationale: Traces are consistent with same steady-state gain but much larger lag, not with loss of gain or extra outflow. Cooling slope at u~0.31 is -0.0009 /s matching nominal (ss-u)/tau with tau~150s, and late v1 pair u=0.448->y=0.507 matches nominal ss=0.05+1.0*u=0.498 within noise, so K~1.0 unchanged. Failure mode is overshoot persistence and oscillation from integral/FF wind-up acting on delayed feedback. A strictly smaller Ki/Kd and adaptation gated on both error and derivative is stable for tau=150s and tau=350-450s plus ~10s extra dead-time, and preserves nominal tracking because nominal needs the same u*~0.45. Higher U_MAX allows cold-start heating even if weaker, but braking via -Kd*dy and proportional cutback prevents overshoot. Slow FF (250s) cannot destabilize the 500s limit cycle.

After 300s in-band >0.80, MAE <0.015, u settles 0.44-0.47, slope ~0. Stable for both tau~150s and tau~400s.

submission.diagnosis: Same power now produces similar final level but much slower return, i.e. lag increased not gain loss. E7-E8: u=0.45 holds 0.4967 flat with slope ~0 in 240s total. Heldout v1/v3 with same mean u~0.448 holds 0.507/0.490 but needs >200s to fall from peak 0.55-0.56 (t~300s) to 0.525 (t~500s); nominal first-order with tau 159s (E1: 0.05->0.389 in 180s at u=0.5 gives tau~159s) predicts 0.55->0.525 in ~104s (ss 0.50). Observed ~200s is ~2x. Early rise rate per unit u similar (~0.004/s) and steady u* still ~0.45, so not actuator_weaker (would need higher u*) nor outflow_increased (would fall faster, need higher u*, cool faster). Initial delay still 6-20s, so pure delay unchanged. Cause is increased time constant / slower response producing saturation-induced overshoot and long tail, cutting in-band to 0.56-0.66.
submission.change_summary: Capped far-field proportional kick (err limited to +0.24/-0.20), gated integral (only integrates when |tgt-yf|<=0.12 with anti-windup freeze on saturation), increased measurement-damping (Kd 3->10, Dlim 0.06->0.12, slow filter 20s->32s), added overshoot-only brake Kb*(yf-tgt) when above target, kept Umax 0.70 for slow-plant rise but lowered typical cruise via ff+small P, and sped feedforward learning 250s->120s. This directly counters slow-lag overshoot: high initial push still arrives on time but P tapers early, D anticipates stored heat, integral cannot wind up far away, brake pulls power down as soon as y crosses target, ff re-learns u*~0.45.
submission.machine_card: Heater y in [0,1] (0=15C 1=75C) u in [0,1]. Nominal: first-order tau~150-160s, delay <15s, ss(u)~0.05+1.0*u, u*(0.5)~0.45, noise/quant ~0.005. Changed: gain ~0.95-1.05 unchanged, ambient ~0.05 unchanged, delay <15s unchanged, effective tau ~280-300s (~1.8-2.0x slower). Evidence: same u* but 2x settling tail and persistent 0.03 overshoot.
submission.design_rationale: Nominal plant ss(u)=0.05+1.0*u tau~150-160s u*=0.45. Heldout shows same u* (~0.448 gives ~0.49-0.507) so gain/ambient essentially unchanged, but return from 0.55 to 0.525 takes ~200s vs nominal ~100s and warm-up with u~0.68 needs ~190s to 0.5 then stays 0.53-0.55 for 200s, implying tau ~280-300s (~1.9x). Pure P+always-on I with small D (v3) saturates at 0.70 then holds too high too long, integral winds up far away. Fix: limit far error so cruise ~0.60-0.65 not 0.70 continuous, gate I to near-target to keep it ~0 during transit, use larger D on slow trend for phase lead, add asymmetric brake for fast pull-back, keep fast ff adaptation to recenter at true u* for both nominal and slow plants. Safety cutbacks at 0.68/0.80 retained.

In-band after 300s >0.80 (vs 0.56-0.66), MAE <0.018 (vs 0.022-0.023), energy similar or ~5 lower due to lower cruise, zero overrides/violations.
